title: Open, Edit, and Save in Photoshop (Day 2): Gradient Sun Rays, PSD Workflow, and JPEG Export
summary: PHLEARN's Day 2 Photoshop tutorial demonstrates a practical workflow for opening various image files, editing with layered gradients to simulate sunlight, and saving and exporting in multiple formats. The instructor walks through opening images via drag-and-drop, the Open dialog, keyboard shortcuts, and recent files; builds a gradient sun effect with a radial gradient on a dedicated layer using the Screen blend mode; samples sky colors with the Eyedropper; creates light rays with a brush on a new layer, applies a radial blur, duplicates and merges layers, then transforms and refines the result with a layer mask. The session emphasizes keeping a layered PSD for future edits and producing a compressed JPEG for sharing, including sRGB conversion and quality settings. The video also contrasts PSD retention with export workflows and previews the topic of file formats in the next lesson.

sections.title: Opening and Accessing Photoshop Documents
concepts: Open dialogue from the splash screen
Open, Open Recent, and keyboard shortcuts
Drag into existing document vs. open as new document (via tabs)
sections.description: The video introduces multiple ways to open images: use the Open dialog, drag files directly into Photoshop, or leverage shortcuts like Ctrl/Cmd+O and Open Recent. It demonstrates initial document handling, including importing a JPEG from the download and previewing how dragging into an existing document creates a new document tab, or dragging onto the tab bar opens a new document. It also notes that recent files appear on the home screen for quick reopening and highlights the dual document model (existing vs new) via the tabbed interface and the Window menu.

sections.title: Gradient Sun Rays: Setup, Colors, and Application
concepts: Applying gradient on a gradient fill layer
sections.description: This section covers building the sun-ray effect with a new gradient fill layer. The instructor selects a radial gradient, changes the foreground color using an Eyedropper to sampled sky tones, and explains gradient types (foreground-to-background and foreground-to-transparent). He demonstrates switching to a radial gradient, applying the gradient by dragging, adjusting its size, and changing the layer’s blend mode from Normal to Screen to create a sunlight glow. The gradient color can be altered at any point, and the gradient layer remains adjustable in opacity and scale.

sections.title: PSD Workflow and Light-Ray Creation
concepts: Saving as PSD to preserve layers
Creating a new layer for light rays
Brush tool usage and color sampling
sections.description: The tutorial emphasizes saving your work as a layered PSD to retain editability, then proceeds to create light rays by painting on a new layer with the Brush tool. The instructor samples sky colors with the Eyedropper, adjusts brush hardness and size, and lays down multiple dots to simulate rays. After laying out the dots, a radial blur filter is introduced to shape the light rays, and options for sharpening or expanding the effect are demonstrated. Duplicating the layer strengthens the effect, and the workflow includes frequent saves to preserve progress.

sections.title: Refinement, Re-Save, and Final Export Considerations
concepts: Layer masking to refine light rays
Exporting for sharing vs. keeping layers
sections.description: The presenter shows how to refine the effect with a layer mask to selectively hide parts of the light rays, then saves the PSD again to preserve the edits. He introduces the export step to prepare a flattened JPEG version for sharing and discusses the distinction between maintaining a PSD for future edits and exporting a compressed image for distribution.

sections.title: Conclusion and Look Ahead
concepts: Next video teaser: file formats overview
sections.description: The video wraps with a quick recap and teases tomorrow's lesson, which will compare PSDs, JPEGs, PNGs, GIFs, and TIFFs among other formats.
